text:
alex-customer: Hey, hitting a weird streaming failure from the Node TS SDK on our Vercel Edge function. Stream starts but stops after ~8-12s, client sees final chunk missing (never gets [DONE]). No 500s, just early close. Using SDK @0.8.9 and Node 18.14 on local tests, same behavior deployed to Vercel edge runtime.

micah-support: sorry about that — can you paste the minimal repro and the response headers you see? is auth token rotating? any 401 logs?

alex-customer: minimal repro below. Not rotating tokens server-side, static API key. On edge we do short-lived key swap for other routes but not this one. No 401s in our logs. Response headers from the edge function: 
`content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`
`cache-control: no-cache`
`connection: keep-alive`

Code: 
```ts
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-small', messages: [{role:'user', content:'long streaming test'}] });
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
}
```

oliver-qa: can you confirm this reproduces locally in the Node runtime (not edge)? you said local looks similar?

alex-customer: local Node shows same hang/early close but less consistently — deployed to Vercel edge it's reliably cutting the stream.

micah-support: thanks. two common things to check: 1) SDK/runtime version mismatch (edge variant vs node variant), 2) abort signal / fetch polyfill differences in edge runtimes. which SDK package did you install exactly? any -edge packages?

alex-customer: package.json lists "@redwood/inference": "0.8.9" (no -edge suffix). We installed via npm.

tara-engineering: aha — 0.8.x predates a fix we shipped for proper stream cancellation and SSE reconnection in edge runtimes. Edge builds (Vercel/Deno) need the runtime-aware client or >=0.9.0 where we moved to fetch-based ReadableStream handling and fixed premature close when middleware rewrites response. The recommended quick test: upgrade to 0.9.2-edge or the latest 0.9.x and try again.

alex-customer: will try upgrading now. any config flags I should flip?

micah-support: set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=stream to see SDK-level stream lifecycle logs. Also on Vercel, ensure you are using the edge runtime (export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }) or the node runtime consistently. If you mix runtimes and use the wrong build of the client, you can end up with unhandled aborts.

alex-customer: after upgrading to 0.9.2-edge and redeploy, streaming seems stable in our Vercel preview — no early close for the longer test. Reduced failures locally too. Thanks!

oliver-qa: can you share the logs (REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=stream) where it used to fail so we can attach to the bug? we want example traces for the regression ticket.

alex-customer: pasted a snippet from the debug log when it failed: 
```
[redwood-sdk][stream] open connection id=0x3fd
[redwood-sdk][stream] received chunk seq=1 len=512
[redwood-sdk][stream] incoming event: keep-alive
[redwood-sdk][stream] fetch aborted by environment: AbortError: The user aborted a request
[redwood-sdk][stream] cleanup triggered, state=closing
```

tara-engineering: perfect — that matches the abort-path we fixed. We'll note the environment abort message. For completeness, could you also confirm whether you were using any middleware that rewrites response headers (edge proxied prerenderers, CDN edge functions)? Those can trigger the same abort in older SDKs.

alex-customer: we do have a simple edge middleware that tags requests for analytics but it doesn't touch response bodies or headers.

micah-support: okay — final notes for the ticket and workaround for other customers: 
- short-term: upgrade to 0.9.2-edge (or >=0.9.1) for edge runtime fixes.
- debug: set REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=stream to capture lifecycle events.
- repro tip: small repro that fails locally: run node 18.14, install @redwood/inference@0.8.9, use the chat.stream code above and let it run for 15s with a prompt that produces long output. Should hit aborts.
- long-term: if you need immediate extra resilience, implement a client-side reconnection loop that resumes from the last stable token/index (we're shipping server-side resume helpers in 0.10).

alex-customer: thanks team — upgrade is working, will keep an eye and let you know if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:

edge-bot: deploy preview finished for pr#842 — status: succeeded.

micah-support: marking this resolved for now, will link to the internal bug 4532 (edge-stream-abort-fix) and close when more telemetry comes in. Thanks for the quick verification!
